```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(SEAC)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(S4Vectors)
```

# Introduction

SEAC performs a KD-tree BLADE mask and a general MaxMin gene-set spatial co-localization analysis for Visium HD. Capture-boundary and non-tissue positions are KD-tree seeds; bins whose nearest seed has Euclidean distance at most one are excluded.

The published BLADE project also includes slide-level artefact tests. SEAC documents its narrower local KD-tree HD mask rather than claiming to implement those additional methods.

# A small SpatialExperiment

```{r toy-data}
counts <- rbind(
    A = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 0L),
    B = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 0L)
)
colnames(counts) <- paste0("bin", 1:8)
coords <- expand.grid(array_row = 1:4, array_col = 1:2)
spe <- SpatialExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(coords, row.names = colnames(counts)),
    spatialCoordsNames = c("array_col", "array_row")
)
sets <- list(left = "A", right = "B")
```

# Score and test

```{r score-and-test}
scored <- maxMinScore(spe, sets)
head(as.data.frame(colData(scored)))

out <- tempfile("seac-permutation-")
tested <- maxMinPermutationTest(
    scored, sets,
    n_permutations = 10L,
    chunk_size = 5L,
    output_dir = out,
    seed = 1L
)
head(loadSEACResults(out))
```

# Space Ranger data

For a standard Space Ranger Visium HD output, use `runSEAC()` with its root,
`outs`, or a `square_XXXum` path. It writes a HDF5-backed
`SpatialExperiment`, a complete audit mask, and a JSON manifest. Supply your
own named `gene_sets`; scored columns and metadata remain available when the
saved post-QC object is reopened in another R session.

Gene sets can contain Ensembl feature IDs or 10x gene symbols. SEAC resolves
the latter from `rowData(qc)$Symbol`, including every feature row that shares a
requested symbol.

```{r spaceranger, eval=FALSE}
gene_sets <- list(
    Paneth = c("LYZ", "DEFA5"),
    Goblet = c("MUC2", "CLCA1")
)

fit <- runSEAC(
    input_dir = "/path/to/spaceranger-output",
    output_dir = "sample_SEAC",
    bin_size = "016",
    gene_sets = gene_sets,
    permutation = TRUE,
    n_permutations = 20L,
    chunk_size = 5L
)

post_qc <- HDF5Array::loadHDF5SummarizedExperiment(
    "sample_SEAC/post_qc/spe"
)
results <- loadSEACResults("sample_SEAC/permutation")
```

Twenty permutations are useful only as a quick workflow smoke test. Use the
default 5,000 or another justified value for a formal analysis.

# Reproducibility

The test stores a manifest and block checkpoints. Re-run the same call with the same output directory and `resume = TRUE` to continue an interrupted job. The random seed is assigned per permutation, so results do not depend on how the 5,000 iterations are chunked.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
